newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech cenbank says watching crown rise closely.
newsitem.headline: Czech cenbank says watching crown rise closely.

text.p: The Czech National Bank said on Friday it was closely watching the recent strong rise of the Czech crown amid a growing trade deficit, but that it was still up to the market to decide its rate.

CNB spokesman Martin Svehla told Reuters that central bank officials were "following the situation, certainly, and are analysing the developments" as the crown moved to a record five percent above parity with its mark/dollar basket on Friday.

Asked whether the CNB might intervene to soften the impact a stronger crown would have on an already large trade deficit, Svehla said that the central bank had widened the crown's fluctuation band to allow the market to decide its rate.
"Within the band, I think movement of the exchange rate is possible, that's why the fluctuation band was widened," he said.
Last February the CNB widenened the corridor within which it fixes the crown each day to plus or minus 7.5 percent from parity with the basket, from plus/minus 0.5 percent.
Since then the foreign exchange market, and not the central bank, has been much more of a force in determining the crown's rate within this controlled float.

The currency has gained nearly three percentage points against the basket since the beginning of the year, mainly on foreign buying to finance a wave of roughly 20 billion crowns in new crown Eurobond issues.

The rise came despite a deteriorating trade deficit which many analysts expect to widen to more than 200 billion crowns in 1997, sending the current account deficit to more than eight percent of gross domestic product.
Svehla said much of the recent crown inflow was in one to two year investments, reflecting the need for financing the Eurobonds.
The CNB, at its last published measurement at the end of November, had foreign currency reserves of $12.6 billion, should it decide to intervene.
